title: elif
goal: In this lesson you will learn elif, another check that runs only if earlier if/elif checks were False.
learn: Add elif between if and else
Stop at the first True branch
idea: elif means "else if." It asks a new question only when the previous if (and earlier elifs) were False. Python checks from top to bottom and runs the first True branch, then skips the rest. Order matters: put the most specific checks first when needed.
changeOneLine: In the editor above, change score = 85 to score = 95. Press Run. Output should be A.

practice.text: Set temp = 15. If temp >= 25 print Hot, elif temp >= 10 print Mild, else print Cold.
practice.hint: Build a chain: if, then elif, then else, all at the same indent. Python picks the first condition that is True.
practice.starterTip: 15 is not hot enough for the first check, but it is >= 10. So the elif branch should print Mild.
practice.gradingNote: Pass if Mild is printed for temp 15 using elif.

practice.text: Set size = "M". If size is S print Small, elif M print Medium, else print Other.
practice.hint: Compare size to strings with ==, like size == "S". Each branch needs a colon and an indented print.
practice.starterTip: Try elif size == "M": with print("Medium") indented under it. Size is already "M".
practice.gradingNote: Pass if Medium prints via elif size == "M".

quiz.question: What does elif mean?
quiz.correct: elif is short for else if.
quiz.wrong: elif = else if: another condition after a failed if.

quiz.question: If the first if is True, do later elifs run?

options.text: No. Python stops at the first True branch

quiz.correct: First True wins; the rest are skipped.
quiz.wrong: Chain stops when one branch matches.

quiz.question: Where does elif go?
quiz.wrong: elif sits between if and the final else.
